content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Sets** as part of **Strings, Arrays, and Collections**. A set models unique elements, so use it when membership and uniqueness matter more than preserving duplicate entries. Use the subtopics—Creating Sets, Uniqueness and Membership, Set Operations—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.
